# Mutants no test can catch, since the program still does just what it did, at most slower.
# `.github/scripts/mutants-equivalent.sh` takes them out of what a run missed. Each entry is four
# lines or more, with a blank line after:
# - the file;
# - what cargo-mutants says the mutant does, after the line and column;
# - the whole line it changes, leading and trailing spaces aside, so the entry goes with the line
#   as code above it moves, and a line changed anywhere is a missed mutant again, to be looked at
#   afresh. Where the same line is written twice in one function, the lines just above it go
#   first, down to it, as many as tell the two apart;
# - why no program can tell the difference.
#
# Add one only when no program could tell the difference. A mutant that only a wrong program
# could show is a missing test, not an equivalent.

crates/llvm/src/lists.rs
delete match arm [] in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::put_in_place
[] => dict == object,
Changes only which lookup's entry the put tries first: `put_found_in_place` writes there only after checking at run time that the lookup searched this very block, and searches again if not, so every put lands in the right entry.

crates/llvm/src/lists.rs

if self
A taken item's local is stored directly only at its own put-back, where the guard already holds, so the guard decides nothing: tried with the item stored into another list, and another field's, before and after its put-back.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
replace + with * in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::undo_case_in_cell
for word in (8..size).step_by(8) {
self.undo_word(cell, offset + word, Word::Plain);
Runs only for a tag that's none of the enum's cases, which no value it holds has: each case puts back its own words in its own block above.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
replace || with && in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::run_crash_cleanup
if !params.is_empty() || !matches!(*returns, Kind::Str) {
Refuses only a cleanup the IR never makes: a crash's cleanup is the checker's own closure, passed to `intrinsics.crash_cleanup`, which takes a `() -> str`, so both sides are false and nothing is refused either way.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
replace match guard self.headers() with true in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::words_of
Kind::Str | Kind::MaybeText if self.headers() => words.push((at, Word::Header)),
Text headers are on in every build: both of `Layouts`' constructors turn them on, and nothing turns them off.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
replace match guard !self.holds_inline(kind) with true in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::words_of
Kind::Enum(_) if !self.holds_inline(kind) => {
Only an enum holding no blocks in place gets here: `undo_in_cell` and `save_words` send one that does to its own case-by-case code first, and the struct arm, the other way in, is never reached.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
delete match arm Kind::Struct(id) in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::words_of
Kind::Struct(id) => {
Never reached: both callers, `undo_in_cell` and `save_words`, take a struct apart field by field themselves, and pass `words_of` only what isn't one.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs

self.words_of(&inner, at + offset, words)?;
In the struct arm, which is never reached: both callers, `undo_in_cell` and `save_words`, take a struct apart field by field themselves.

crates/llvm/src/rollback.rs
replace match guard kind.counted() with true in Emit<'_, '_, '_>::words_of
_ if kind.counted() => words.push((at, Word::Block)),
The one kind that gets here uncounted is `Unit`, and no field holds one: a program keeping a value of type `nothing` isn't lowered, so it never builds.

crates/llvm/src/share.rs
replace < with <= in moves
at != 0 && at < Span::PRELUDE
Also counts a place at exactly `Span::PRELUDE` as moving, and none is there: that's byte 0 of the first library file, `errors.fen`, which opens with a doc comment the lexer skips, so no token, and no instruction, starts at it.

crates/llvm/src/share.rs
replace Share::keeping -> bool with true
self.added.is_some()
Only has a build that keeps no units call `add` anyway: with nothing kept, `add` keeps nothing and `add_places` finds no table, and the layouts note no reads, so nothing a build writes changes.
